answer: Home load calculators add up what your appliances draw and use: running watts, the peak with a motor starting, amps, daily and monthly units and what they cost. Use them before adding an AC, before sizing solar, a UPS or a generator, or to check whether your connection's sanctioned load is enough.

sections.h2: Which load calculator do I need?
p: For the whole house, the [[E1|home electrical load calculator]]; for one appliance or a short list, the [[E2|appliance load calculator]]; for the current on a single-phase supply, the [[E3|single phase load calculator]]. Before buying an AC, the [[E4|load check before adding an AC]] shows whether the connection takes it.

To turn watts into units, use the [[E6|unit calculator]], or for an AC the [[E5|AC units calculator]]. For running costs and choices: [[N10|inverter vs non-inverter AC payback]], [[N9|AC temperature saving]], [[N5|winter heating cost]], [[N8|e-bike charging cost]] and the [[N7|UPS vs solar vs generator cost]] per backup hour.

Watts are the rate of use at a moment; units (kWh) are watts × hours ÷ one thousand and are what the bill charges for. The default home on the home load calculator draws {{pg.E1.out.running_w|int}} W while everything on its list runs and uses about {{pg.E1.out.monthly_units|int}} units a month; the [[F1|electricity bill calculator]] turns units into rupees.

faq.q: How do I calculate my home's electrical load?
faq.a: Add the running watts of everything that can be on at the same time, taken from each label or the [[H2|appliance list]], and divide by volts × power factor for the amps. The [[E1|home electrical load calculator]] does it from a list.

faq.q: How many units does an AC use?
faq.a: It depends on its tonnage, whether it is an inverter model, the room and the hours. The [[E5|AC units calculator]] gives the units per hour and per month for your AC, and the [[N16|AC bill calculator]] what it adds to the whole bill.

faq.q: What is the difference between connected load and sanctioned load?
faq.a: Connected load is everything installed; sanctioned load is the kW your DISCO agreed to supply, worked out from the connected load with a diversity factor because not everything runs at once. The [[N4|sanctioned load calculator]] does it.

faq.q: Does an inverter AC save money?
faq.a: It uses fewer units than a non-inverter AC of the same size once the room is cool, and the saving grows with the hours it runs and the tariff. The [[N10|inverter AC payback calculator]] works out how soon its higher price pays back.
